research_updates.notes: Sources and searches covered AEDC QACF/Act 1282 annual reports and transparency pages, DFA business-incentive cost reports, Arkansas Transparency FY2013-2026 expenditures/contracts, Arkansas Legislative Audit results, Little Rock FY2010-FY2026 budgets/ACFRs/monthly reports, Board agendas/minutes/attachments, City Wallet/check-register references, Tax Back endorsements, EMMA/official statements and bond/PILOT/TIF/IRB terms. The material QACF report records $1 million Windstream payments on 2010-07-19 and 2011-06-16 for Little Rock building renovations/equipment; only the first safely excludes this parcel by predating its 2011-02-25 acquisition. A companion AEDC activity report crosswalks a Windstream Corporate Headquarters project to QACF but supplies no payment identifiers or address, so the post-acquisition June 2011 payment remains ambiguous and neither payment is assigned to this project. Third-party indexes show company-level Hosted Solutions/TierPoint tax-credit entries without site, period or agreement; underlying public reports did not provide a selected-facility allocation. research_updates.title: Environmental, utility and infrastructure audit — backup equipment separated from one-side engineering sensitivities
research_updates.notes: Arkansas DEQ Permit Data System, RST billing/facility pages and Environment FeatureServer layers were searched by AFIN 60-04506/6004506, permit 60002155, facility name WINDSTREAM, owner TIERPOINT LLC, exact address and operator aliases; EPA ECHO/FRS, APSC, Entergy Arkansas, Central Arkansas Water and Little Rock Water Reclamation Authority portals were separately queried for 2010-2026 with outcomes recorded in their own sources. The exact DEQ match lists two 4,000-gallon diesel ASTs mounted above generators, no USTs or tank leaks, and paid facility fees from 2012-2023; the catalog has no regulatory-fee metric, so the exact ledger is retained as non-canonical. TierPoint reports two 2.25 MW generators, dual 3,000 kVA utility transformers and true 2N UPS, while the assessor inventory describes two 2,500 kW generators; the definitions/date conflict is preserved. The synthesis uses only one non-additive 3,000 kVA redundancy side. Its real-power sensitivity is 3 MVA x assumed PF 0.8/0.9/1.0 = 2.4/2.7/3.0 MW. Its annual IT-energy sensitivity is 3 MVA x PF x utilization x 8,760 / PUE, using correlated low/central/high bundles of PF 0.8/0.9/1.0, utilization 25%/50%/75% and PUE 2.0/1.6/1.2, yielding 2.628/7.39125/16.425 million kWh. These are visibly modeled engineering sensitivities, not contracted capacity, actual load, metered use or critical IT capacity. The second 2N side, 85 kW per-cabinet maximum, generators and tank volume are excluded from the arithmetic.

research_updates.title: Investment, construction, supplier and operating-model decisions — conditional coverage floor retained
research_updates.notes: Investment candidate: converting 'multimillion-dollar,' the 2011 $2.697 million property purchase, 2014/2015 sale-leaseback prices or the $575 million portfolio sale into facility capital investment is rejected because the first is unbounded, deed prices are asset transfers and the portfolio price has no site allocation. Construction candidate: the rejected $5,000 right-of-way application cannot be summed or multiplied, and the opening-era retrofit lacks issued-permit value, audited outlay, asset mix, duration, workers, hours, payroll and local residence. Supplier/indirect candidate: applying an input-output multiplier or transferred local-purchase share is rejected because no eligible direct-spend base, paid vendor amount, multiplier vintage/geography or channel separation exists. Operations candidate: the facility-specific 2012 release says the onsite NOC was staffed 24/7/365, necessarily describing at least one occupied coverage position at any instant. The synthesis therefore retains the zero-leave arithmetic floor of 8,760 coverage hours / (40 hours x 52 weeks) = 4.211538 FTE-equivalents. It is not employee headcount, payroll, resident employment or a current staffing snapshot; employment versus contractor status, multiple simultaneous posts, relief coverage, leave, occupation, wages and residence remain unknown. No relief factor or wage multiplier is applied.

A public-service-cost break-even remains rejected because no verified same-recipient revenue exists; incentive and community candidates remain unallocated.

research_updates.title: GDP, employment and wage outcome decisions — 2012 is not a clean county treatment
research_updates.notes: The governed BEA/BLS county panel for Pulaski County FIPS 05119 was reviewed over 2001-2024 with candidate pre-periods ending in 2011, a 2012 opening anchor and possible post-periods through 2024. GDP candidate: difference-in-differences, event-study and synthetic-control approaches are rejected because the selected building was already a 1993 computer center, Acxiom had another Little Rock data center by fiscal 2006, the treatment intensity is unknown and concurrent headquarters/sector shocks cannot be separated. Employment candidate: the same timing and donor failures apply, and neither the current vacancy nor corporate headcounts measure facility or county job contribution. Wage candidate: the same identification failures apply; no facility payroll or occupation mix exists and county nominal average weekly wages mix inflation and industry composition. A descriptive county gap is also rejected as insufficiently decision-relevant because it cannot distinguish this small retrofit/operation from the diverse county economy. No county comparison is presented as a project effect and no public-records requests or other solicitations were made.

source.title: Pulaski County economic-panel and treatment-design audit
source.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis / U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
source.notes: Repository county economic panels derived from official BEA real-GDP and BLS QCEW employment and nominal average-weekly-wage series were reviewed for Pulaski County FIPS 05119 over 2001-2024. Candidate pre-periods ending in 2011 and post-periods beginning in 2012 were considered. The selected property was already a 1993 computer center; Acxiom operated a separate Little Rock data center by fiscal 2006; Windstream's headquarters retention/expansion and multiple other county shocks overlap the proposed treatment; and no facility investment, payroll or stable exposure intensity is available. These failures apply separately to GDP, employment and wage outcomes and defeat difference-in-differences, event-study, synthetic-control and project-effect interpretations; a descriptive gap is also rejected as insufficiently decision-relevant because it cannot isolate the selected project.

modeled_syntheses.label: Zero-leave minimum continuous-coverage FTE-equivalent

period.label: Conditional annual coverage equivalent from the 2012 onsite NOC staffing statement

scope.label: At least one continuously occupied onsite NOC coverage position at the Windstream/TierPoint Little Rock data center; employment relationship unallocated

interval.interpretation: Mathematical zero-leave lower bound conditional on the facility-specific statement that the onsite NOC was staffed 24/7/365; not observed employee headcount.

provenance.detail: Facility-specific statement that the onsite network operations center was staffed 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year
Forty scheduled hours per week for 52 weeks, with zero leave, training, breaks, overlap, or relief allowance

modeled_syntheses.confidence_rationale: The continuous onsite staffing statement is facility-specific and the division is exact. The result is conditional and cannot distinguish employees from contractors, actual headcount, multiple simultaneous posts, leave relief, residence, occupation, or payroll.
modeled_syntheses.decision_relevance: Provides a conservative floor for the labor coverage embodied by a documented 24x7 onsite operating function without inflating it with an unsourced relief factor or relabeling it as people employed.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Actual headcount, employer/contractor status, simultaneous posts, schedules, relief coverage, leave, occupations, payroll, and worker residence

derivation.formula: 24 hours/day × 365 days/year ÷ (40 hours/week × 52 weeks/year)
assumptions: At least one onsite NOC coverage position was continuously occupied as the operator statement says.
One zero-leave FTE-equivalent supplies 2,080 scheduled hours per year.
No relief factor or multiplier is applied.

limitations: FTE-equivalent coverage is not employee headcount or payroll.
Employment relationship, contractor status, worker residence, occupation, wages, benefits, and actual staffing levels are unknown.
Real operations require breaks, leave, training, overlap, and relief, so actual labor supporting one continuous post would exceed this zero-leave floor.
The 2012 statement does not establish persistence at the same staffing arrangement in later years.
modeled_syntheses.notes: Conditional mathematical lower bound only. Do not count as observed employees, filled jobs, resident employment, or a current staffing snapshot.

project_description: TierPoint's Little Rock data center operates at 15707 Chenal Parkway in Little Rock, Pulaski County, Arkansas, in a 1993 building the assessor classifies as a 30,970-square-foot computer center. Windstream Hosted Solutions bought the parcel in February 2011 and announced the 30,000-square-foot center open on April 12, 2012; TierPoint took over the data-center business in December 2015 and the current parcel owner is TierPoint Properties LLC. Current and archived operator specifications report 30,000+ total square feet, a nested 9,000+ raised-floor/data-center-space subset, true 2N UPS, dual 3,000 kVA utility transformers, and two redundant 2.25 MW generators with 4,000 gallons of fuel storage each, while state records independently register the two tanks. Historic planning and business listings reused 15707 for an adjacent trampoline/car-wash property now numbered 15701, so address-only records are not assigned to this project without a parcel or facility crosswalk.
